description: Design and implement an ETL pipeline from source systems to a target data store.

steps.description: Inventory all source systems, data formats, and access methods.

inputs.name: source-systems
inputs.desc: List of source systems to connect to

inputs.name: data-requirements
inputs.desc: What data is needed and why

outputs.name: source-catalog
outputs.desc: Catalog of all source systems with formats and access methods

process: List every source system and its data format (relational, API, flat file, streaming).
Document access methods, authentication, and rate limits for each source.
Build the data dictionary with field names, types, and cardinality.
Identify data freshness requirements and update frequencies.

steps.description: Map source schemas to the target schema with transformation rules.

inputs.name: source-catalog
inputs.desc: Catalog of source systems and their schemas

inputs.name: target-schema
inputs.desc: Target data store schema or requirements

outputs.name: mapping-exceptions
outputs.desc: Fields that require special handling or business rules

process: Map each source field to its target field with data type conversions.
Define transformation rules for fields that require cleaning or enrichment.
Document business rules for derived fields and aggregations.
Flag fields with no direct mapping for resolution.

steps.description: Design the extraction strategy for each source system.

outputs.name: extraction-plan
outputs.desc: Extraction strategy per source (full, incremental, CDC)

outputs.name: extraction-schedule
outputs.desc: Timing and frequency for each extraction

process: Select full load vs incremental vs change data capture for each source.
Define the change detection mechanism (timestamp, sequence, log-based).
Set extraction windows to minimize source system impact.
Plan error handling and retry logic for each extraction.

steps.description: Implement the data transformations: cleaning, normalization, and enrichment.

inputs.name: extraction-plan
inputs.desc: How data is extracted from each source

process: Implement data cleaning rules (nulls, duplicates, format standardization).
Build normalization steps (unit conversion, encoding, date formatting).
Add enrichment logic (lookups, derived fields, aggregations).
Write test cases for each transformation covering edge cases.

steps.description: Define the load strategy for writing data to the target store.

outputs.name: load-plan
outputs.desc: Load strategy (upsert, append, SCD type) per table

outputs.name: load-validation-rules
outputs.desc: Rules to validate data after loading

process: Select the load pattern per table: append, upsert, or slowly changing dimension.
Define the merge keys and conflict resolution rules.
Plan the load order to respect foreign key constraints.
Set up post-load validation (row counts, checksums, referential integrity).

steps.description: Set up scheduling, orchestration, and monitoring for the pipeline.

outputs.name: monitoring-alerts
outputs.desc: Alert rules for pipeline failures and SLA breaches

process: Define the pipeline DAG with dependencies between extraction, transformation, and load.
Configure the scheduler (cron, event-driven, or hybrid).
Set up monitoring for job duration, row counts, and error rates.
Configure alerting for failures and SLA breaches.

steps.description: Produce the pipeline design document with all specifications.
process: Compile source-to-target mappings, extraction strategies, and load plans.
Document the orchestration DAG and scheduling details.
Write the operational runbook with troubleshooting procedures.
Include data lineage diagrams and dependency maps.

description: Engineer and validate features for a machine learning model from raw data.

steps.description: Explore the raw dataset to understand distributions, types, and quality.

outputs.name: quality-issues
outputs.desc: List of data quality issues found

process: Compute summary statistics for every column (mean, median, std, min, max, nulls).
Visualize distributions and identify skewness or multimodality.
Check for class imbalance in the target variable.
Identify columns with high cardinality, constant values, or excessive nulls.

steps.description: Identify candidate features from domain knowledge and data patterns.

inputs.name: domain-context
inputs.desc: Domain knowledge about what signals matter

outputs.name: candidate-features
outputs.desc: List of candidate features with rationale

outputs.name: feature-hypotheses
outputs.desc: Hypotheses about which features will be predictive

process: List features suggested by domain knowledge and prior research.
Identify potential interaction terms and polynomial features.
Define time-based features (lags, rolling windows, trends) if applicable.
Document the rationale for each candidate feature.

steps.description: Compute the candidate features from raw data.

outputs.name: computation-log
outputs.desc: Log of how each feature was computed

process: Compute aggregation features (counts, sums, averages by group).
Compute ratio and interaction features.
Compute time-based features (lags, rolling statistics, time since event).
Log the computation method for each feature for reproducibility.

steps.description: Assess feature importance and remove redundant or irrelevant features.
process: Compute univariate importance (mutual information, chi-squared, ANOVA F-test).
Run a tree-based model and extract feature importances.
Compute pairwise correlations and flag highly correlated pairs.
Remove features with near-zero variance or near-perfect correlation.

steps.description: Handle missing values and outliers in the feature set.

inputs.name: feature-matrix
inputs.desc: Feature matrix with potential missing values

outputs.name: clean-feature-matrix
outputs.desc: Feature matrix with missing values and outliers handled

outputs.name: imputation-report
outputs.desc: How each missing value and outlier was handled

process: Classify missing data patterns (MCAR, MAR, MNAR).
Select imputation strategy per feature (median, mode, KNN, model-based, or drop).
Detect outliers using IQR, z-score, or isolation forest.
Apply capping, transformation, or removal for outliers.

steps.description: Validate feature distributions on train vs test and produce the report.

outputs.name: validated-feature-set
outputs.desc: Final validated feature set ready for modeling

process: Split into train and test sets and compare distributions (KS test, PSI).
Check for data leakage (features computed from future or target information).
Produce the final feature set with documentation.
Write the feature engineering report with decisions and rationale.

description: Train a machine learning model from data splitting through evaluation and experiment logging.

steps.description: Split data into train, validation, and test sets with proper stratification.
process: Select the split strategy based on data characteristics (random, time-based, group).
Apply stratification to preserve class distribution.
Verify no data leakage between splits.
Document the split ratios and random seeds for reproducibility.

steps.description: Select candidate algorithms based on the problem type and data characteristics.

inputs.name: train-set
inputs.desc: Training data to evaluate algorithms on

process: Classify the problem type and select appropriate algorithm families.
Run each candidate with default parameters on a validation fold.
Record baseline scores (accuracy, RMSE, AUC depending on problem type).
Select the top candidates for hyperparameter tuning.

steps.description: Tune hyperparameters for the selected algorithms.

outputs.name: tuning-results
outputs.desc: Results from all hyperparameter combinations tried

process: Define the search space for each algorithm's hyperparameters.
Run the search (grid, random, or Bayesian optimization) with cross-validation.
Track all trials with parameters and scores.
Select the best configuration per algorithm.

steps.description: Train the final model on the full training set with the best hyperparameters.

outputs.name: training-metadata
outputs.desc: Training duration, convergence, and resource usage

process: Train the final model on the full training set.
Monitor convergence and training loss.
Save the model artifact with versioning.
Record training metadata (duration, resource usage, final loss).

steps.description: Evaluate the trained model on the held-out test set.

outputs.name: evaluation-metrics
outputs.desc: Performance metrics on the test set

outputs.name: error-analysis
outputs.desc: Analysis of where the model fails

process: Run predictions on the test set.
Compute metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, AUC (classification) or RMSE, MAE, R-squared (regression).
Generate confusion matrix or residual plots.
Analyze error patterns by segment or feature range.

steps.description: Log the experiment with all parameters, metrics, and artifacts.
process: Log the experiment to the tracking system (MLflow, Weights and Biases).
Record parameters, metrics, and the model artifact.
Tag the experiment with the dataset version and code commit.
Write the training report with methodology and results.

description: Deploy a trained machine learning model to production with serving infrastructure.

steps.description: Package the trained model for deployment.

outputs.name: packaged-model
outputs.desc: Model packaged for the target environment

process: Serialize the model in the target format (ONNX, TorchScript, SavedModel, pickle).
Build the inference container or package with all dependencies.
Include preprocessing and postprocessing code alongside the model.
Verify the package produces correct predictions in isolation.

steps.description: Set up the serving infrastructure for the model.
process: Select the serving framework (TF Serving, Triton, FastAPI, SageMaker).
Configure compute resources based on latency and throughput requirements.
Set up health checks and readiness probes.
Deploy the initial version with monitoring enabled.

steps.description: Implement input validation and preprocessing for the serving endpoint.
process: Define the input schema with type and range constraints.
Implement validation that rejects malformed requests with clear error messages.
Add preprocessing to match the training pipeline (scaling, encoding).
Test with valid, invalid, and edge-case inputs.

steps.description: Configure autoscaling for the serving infrastructure.

outputs.name: cost-estimate
outputs.desc: Estimated infrastructure cost at different traffic levels

process: Define scaling metrics (CPU, memory, request queue depth, latency).
Set minimum and maximum replica counts.
Configure scale-up and scale-down thresholds and cooldown periods.
Estimate costs at expected and peak traffic levels.

steps.description: Set up A/B traffic splitting for safe model rollout.

inputs.name: rollout-strategy
inputs.desc: How to roll out the new model (canary, blue-green, shadow)

process: Configure the traffic split between the current and new model versions.
Define the rollout stages (1%, 10%, 50%, 100%) with success criteria at each.
Set up comparison metrics between model versions.
Define the automatic rollback trigger conditions.

steps.description: Produce the deployment runbook with rollback procedures.
process: Document the full deployment procedure step by step.
Write the rollback procedure for each deployment stage.
Include monitoring dashboards and alert channels to watch.
Document the on-call escalation path for deployment issues.

description: Design, run, and analyze an A/B test from hypothesis through statistical analysis.

steps.description: Define the hypothesis, success metric, and guardrail metrics.

outputs.name: experiment-hypothesis
outputs.desc: Formal hypothesis with primary and guardrail metrics

process: State the null and alternative hypotheses.
Define the primary success metric with its precise calculation.
Define guardrail metrics that must not degrade.
Set the minimum detectable effect size based on business value.

steps.description: Calculate the required sample size using power analysis.

outputs.name: experiment-duration
outputs.desc: Expected time to reach required sample size

process: Compute the required sample size given alpha, power, and minimum effect.
Account for the metric's variance and any clustering effects.
Estimate how long it takes to accumulate the required sample at current traffic.
Adjust for expected attrition or exclusions.

steps.description: Design the randomization and assignment mechanism.

outputs.name: randomization-plan
outputs.desc: How users are assigned to variants

outputs.name: assignment-config
outputs.desc: Technical configuration for the assignment system

process: Select the randomization unit (user, session, device, region).
Design the assignment mechanism (hash-based, feature flag, CDN).
Plan for holdout and exclusion groups.
Verify the assignment produces balanced groups (A/A test or simulation).

steps.description: Monitor the running experiment for problems.

inputs.name: metric-definitions
inputs.desc: Metrics to track during the experiment

outputs.name: monitoring-report
outputs.desc: Daily monitoring checks during the experiment

outputs.name: sample-ratio-check
outputs.desc: Verification that assignment ratios are correct

process: Check for sample ratio mismatch daily (chi-squared test).
Monitor guardrail metrics for unexpected degradation.
Check for novelty effects or time-based trends.
Flag any instrumentation issues or data collection gaps.

steps.description: Analyze experiment results with proper statistical methods.

outputs.name: statistical-results
outputs.desc: Test statistics, p-values, and confidence intervals

outputs.name: segment-analysis
outputs.desc: Results broken down by key segments

process: Compute the treatment effect with confidence intervals.
Run the statistical test (t-test, Mann-Whitney, or Bayesian posterior).
Correct for multiple comparisons if testing multiple metrics.
Break down results by pre-defined segments.

steps.description: Produce the experiment report with the decision recommendation.

outputs.name: ship-decision
outputs.desc: Ship, iterate, or kill recommendation with rationale

process: Summarize the treatment effect on primary and guardrail metrics.
Highlight any notable segment differences.
Make the ship/iterate/kill recommendation with supporting evidence.
Document lessons learned for future experiments.

description: Set up automated data quality monitoring with rules, dashboards, and alerting.

steps.description: Profile the data to establish quality baselines.

outputs.name: baseline-profile
outputs.desc: Statistical baselines for each column and table

process: Compute column-level statistics (nulls, cardinality, min, max, distribution).
Compute table-level statistics (row counts, freshness, schema changes).
Identify historical patterns and seasonal variations.
Establish baseline thresholds for each quality dimension.

steps.description: Define quality rules for completeness, uniqueness, freshness, and conformance.
process: Define completeness rules (null rate thresholds per column).
Define uniqueness rules (duplicate detection on key columns).
Define freshness rules (maximum staleness per dataset).
Define conformance rules (schema, format, range, referential integrity).

steps.description: Implement automated quality checks in the data pipeline.

outputs.name: check-implementation
outputs.desc: Automated quality checks integrated into the pipeline

process: Implement each rule as an automated check (Great Expectations, dbt tests, custom SQL).
Configure checks to run at ingestion, transformation, and load stages.
Set pass/fail thresholds and warning thresholds.
Test each check against known good and known bad data.

steps.description: Configure alerting thresholds and notification channels.

outputs.name: escalation-policy
outputs.desc: Who gets notified at each severity level

process: Set critical vs warning thresholds for each check.
Route alerts by severity to appropriate channels (email, Slack, PagerDuty).
Define the escalation policy for unresolved alerts.
Configure alert suppression to avoid noise during planned maintenance.

steps.description: Build the data quality dashboard for visibility.

outputs.name: quality-scorecard
outputs.desc: Summary score per dataset and dimension

process: Build summary views showing pass/fail rates per dataset.
Add trend charts for each quality dimension over time.
Include drill-down to individual rule results.
Create the quality scorecard with color-coded health indicators.

steps.description: Define the incident response process for data quality failures.
process: Define the triage process for data quality alerts.
Document common failure modes and their resolution steps.
Set SLAs for investigation and resolution by severity.
Write the complete monitoring plan document.

description: Set up monitoring to detect and respond to model drift in production.

steps.description: Define the metrics to monitor for prediction, feature, and concept drift.

inputs.name: model-info
inputs.desc: The deployed model and its training data characteristics

inputs.name: business-metrics
inputs.desc: Business metrics tied to model performance

outputs.name: drift-metrics
outputs.desc: Defined drift metrics and their calculation methods

process: Define prediction drift metrics (output distribution shift, confidence score changes).
Define feature drift metrics (input distribution shift per feature).
Define concept drift indicators (performance degradation on labeled samples).
Store the training data distributions as the reference baseline.

steps.description: Implement statistical tests for drift detection.
process: Implement PSI (Population Stability Index) for categorical and binned features.
Implement KS test for continuous feature distributions.
Implement Jensen-Shannon divergence for prediction distributions.
Set thresholds based on acceptable drift levels.

steps.description: Set up automated drift monitoring on production data.

inputs.name: production-data-source
inputs.desc: Where to collect production predictions and inputs

outputs.name: drift-dashboard
outputs.desc: Dashboard showing drift metrics over time

process: Configure the data collection from production (predictions, inputs, ground truth).
Schedule drift tests at regular intervals (hourly, daily, weekly).
Build the drift dashboard with time series for each metric.
Set window sizes for comparison (daily vs weekly vs monthly).

steps.description: Configure alerting for detected drift.

outputs.name: response-playbook
outputs.desc: Playbook for responding to drift alerts

process: Define alert severity levels (warning, critical) based on drift magnitude.
Route alerts to the ML engineering team.
Write the response playbook (investigate, retrain, rollback).
Set up automatic report generation when drift is detected.

steps.description: Define the criteria and process for triggering model retraining.
process: Define the retraining triggers (drift score thresholds, performance degradation, schedule).
Document the retraining pipeline (data refresh, training, evaluation, deployment).
Set the approval process for retraining (automatic vs manual review).
Write the complete drift monitoring plan.

description: Design and implement a data lakehouse with bronze, silver, and gold layers.

steps.description: Design the storage layers (bronze, silver, gold) and their purposes.

inputs.name: use-cases
inputs.desc: Analytics and ML use cases to support

outputs.name: layer-design
outputs.desc: Design for bronze, silver, and gold layers

process: Define the bronze layer: raw ingestion, append-only, schema-on-read.
Define the silver layer: cleaned, conformed, deduplicated, schema-on-write.
Define the gold layer: business-level aggregates and feature stores.
Map each use case to the layer it reads from.

steps.description: Select the storage format and table format for the lakehouse.

inputs.name: query-patterns
inputs.desc: Expected query patterns and performance needs

outputs.name: format-selection
outputs.desc: Selected file and table formats per layer

outputs.name: partitioning-strategy
outputs.desc: Partitioning and clustering strategy per table

process: Evaluate file formats (Parquet, ORC, Avro) against query patterns.
Select the table format (Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, Apache Hudi).
Design the partitioning strategy per table based on query filters.
Plan compaction and optimization schedules.

steps.description: Implement the ingestion layer for getting data into the lakehouse.
process: Build connectors for each source system (batch, streaming, CDC).
Implement schema evolution handling for source changes.
Set up dead letter queues for failed records.
Configure the ingestion schedule and monitoring.

steps.description: Set up the query engine for analytics and ML workloads.
process: Select and configure the query engine (Spark, Trino, DuckDB, Databricks SQL).
Set up resource pools for different workload types.
Run benchmark queries and tune for acceptable performance.
Configure caching and materialized views for frequent queries.

steps.description: Configure access controls, governance, and lineage tracking.
process: Configure table-level and column-level access controls.
Set up data lineage tracking (column-level lineage through transformations).
Implement data retention and purge policies.
Configure audit logging for all data access.

steps.description: Produce the lakehouse architecture document.
process: Compile the architecture design with layer descriptions and data flows.
Document the governance model and access control policies.
Write the operations runbook (compaction, optimization, troubleshooting).
Include cost estimates and capacity planning guidance.

description: Build a recommendation system from data collection through online evaluation.

steps.description: Collect and prepare user interaction data for the recommendation model.

inputs.name: interaction-logs
inputs.desc: Raw user interaction data (views, clicks, purchases)

process: Extract relevant interactions (implicit: views, clicks; explicit: ratings).
Filter out bots, test accounts, and low-activity users.
Build the user-item interaction matrix.
Compute sparsity, popularity distribution, and cold-start statistics.

steps.description: Select the recommendation approach based on data characteristics.

outputs.name: approach-rationale
outputs.desc: Why this approach fits the data

process: Evaluate collaborative filtering feasibility (density, user overlap).
Assess content-based feasibility (item feature availability).
Consider hybrid approaches for cold-start mitigation.
Document the approach selection rationale.

steps.description: Train the recommendation model.
process: Split data by time (train on older, evaluate on newer interactions).
Train the model (matrix factorization, neural CF, two-tower, or content-based).
Tune hyperparameters (embedding size, learning rate, regularization).
Save the trained model and user/item embeddings.

steps.description: Evaluate the model with offline metrics.

outputs.name: coverage-analysis
outputs.desc: Item coverage and popularity bias analysis

process: Compute ranking metrics: precision@k, recall@k, NDCG, MAP.
Measure item coverage (what fraction of items get recommended).
Analyze popularity bias (does the model only recommend popular items).
Compare against baseline (most popular, random).

steps.description: Implement the serving layer for real-time recommendations.

outputs.name: serving-config
outputs.desc: Caching, filtering, and business rule configuration

process: Deploy the model for real-time inference (precomputed or on-the-fly).
Add business rules (filtering already purchased, enforcing diversity).
Configure caching for frequently requested recommendations.
Set up fallback strategies for cold-start users.

steps.description: Set up online evaluation to measure real user engagement.

outputs.name: online-experiment
outputs.desc: A/B test configuration for the recommender

process: Set up an A/B test comparing the new model against the current system.
Define online metrics (CTR, conversion rate, revenue per session, diversity).
Monitor for position bias and presentation effects.
Write the recommendation system report with offline and online results.

description: Plan and execute a data migration from a source system to a target system.

steps.description: Inventory the source data including schemas, volumes, and dependencies.

inputs.name: source-system
inputs.desc: The source system to migrate from

inputs.name: migration-scope
inputs.desc: What data is in scope for migration

process: Catalog all tables, views, and stored procedures in scope.
Document row counts, data sizes, and growth rates.
Map foreign key and application-level dependencies.
Identify data that should be archived vs migrated.

steps.description: Map source schemas to the target system schema.

inputs.name: target-system
inputs.desc: The target system and its schema requirements

outputs.name: transformation-rules
outputs.desc: Data transformation rules for the migration

process: Map each source table and column to its target equivalent.
Define transformations for data type changes and format differences.
Handle schema differences (split tables, merged tables, renamed columns).
Document fields with no target mapping and their disposition.

steps.description: Design the migration strategy (big bang, phased, or parallel run).

outputs.name: rollback-plan
outputs.desc: Plan to roll back if migration fails

process: Evaluate big bang vs phased vs parallel run based on risk tolerance and downtime.
If phased, define the migration order respecting dependencies.
Plan the data sync mechanism during parallel run (if applicable).
Design the rollback procedure for each phase.

steps.description: Implement and test the migration scripts.

outputs.name: test-results
outputs.desc: Results from test runs on sample data

process: Write extraction scripts for each source table.
Implement transformations per the mapping rules.
Write load scripts for the target system.
Run on a representative sample and validate correctness.

steps.description: Validate data integrity after migration.

outputs.name: validation-results
outputs.desc: Row counts, checksums, and spot check results

outputs.name: discrepancy-report
outputs.desc: Any discrepancies found and their resolution

process: Compare row counts between source and target for every table.
Compute checksums on key columns and compare.
Run spot checks on random samples comparing field values.
Verify referential integrity in the target system.

steps.description: Plan the cutover window and produce the migration plan document.
process: Schedule the cutover window with stakeholder agreement.
Build the minute-by-minute cutover checklist.
Define the go/no-go criteria at each checkpoint.
Compile the complete migration plan document.

description: Build an NLP text processing pipeline from corpus preparation through deployment.

steps.description: Collect and prepare the text corpus for NLP processing.

inputs.name: task-definition
inputs.desc: The NLP task (classification, NER, sentiment, etc.)

outputs.name: corpus-statistics
outputs.desc: Document count, vocabulary size, class distribution

process: Collect text documents from all sources.
Clean the text (remove HTML, fix encoding, normalize whitespace).
Label or annotate the corpus for the target task.
Compute corpus statistics (document count, vocabulary size, class balance).

steps.description: Implement text preprocessing (tokenization, normalization, stop words).
process: Tokenize the text (word-level, subword, or character depending on task).
Apply normalization (lowercasing, lemmatization or stemming).
Remove stop words (if appropriate for the task).
Handle special tokens, numbers, and domain-specific vocabulary.

steps.description: Extract features from the preprocessed text.

outputs.name: feature-method
outputs.desc: Which extraction method was used and why

process: Select the feature extraction method (TF-IDF, word embeddings, sentence embeddings).
For TF-IDF: fit the vectorizer and transform the corpus.
For embeddings: load or train the embedding model (Word2Vec, FastText, BERT).
Validate feature dimensionality and coverage.

steps.description: Train the NLP model for the target task.

outputs.name: training-history
outputs.desc: Loss and metric curves during training

process: Split into train, validation, and test sets.
Train the model (logistic regression, SVM, LSTM, transformer fine-tuning).
Monitor validation metrics during training to prevent overfitting.
Select the best checkpoint based on validation performance.

steps.description: Evaluate the NLP model on the test set.

outputs.name: error-examples
outputs.desc: Examples of model errors for analysis

process: Run predictions on the held-out test set.
Compute task-specific metrics (classification: F1, accuracy; NER: entity F1; generation: BLEU).
Analyze error patterns (which classes or entity types fail).
Collect representative error examples for review.

steps.description: Deploy the NLP pipeline and produce the report.
process: Package the preprocessing and model into a single inference pipeline.
Deploy with input validation and error handling.
Set up monitoring for prediction distribution and latency.
Write the NLP pipeline report with methodology, results, and limitations.

description: Implement a data catalog for discovery, governance, and lineage tracking.

steps.description: Inventory all data assets across the organization.

inputs.name: data-systems
inputs.desc: List of data systems to catalog

process: Connect to each data system and extract schema metadata.
Catalog databases, tables, columns, views, and APIs.
Record data types, constraints, and relationships.
Identify undocumented or shadow IT data stores.

steps.description: Define the metadata schema with technical, business, and operational dimensions.

outputs.name: metadata-schema
outputs.desc: Defined metadata schema for the catalog

process: Define technical metadata fields (schema, type, format, size, freshness).
Define business metadata fields (description, owner, domain, use cases).
Define operational metadata (SLAs, quality scores, access frequency).
Create the classification taxonomy (domain, sensitivity, criticality).

steps.description: Populate metadata for each data asset.
process: Auto-populate technical metadata from system connections.
Collect business metadata from data owners through intake forms.
Apply classification labels using automated rules and manual review.
Identify and track gaps in metadata coverage.

steps.description: Implement search and discovery functionality.

outputs.name: discovery-features
outputs.desc: Faceted search, recommendations, and popular assets

process: Index all metadata for full-text and faceted search.
Implement filtering by domain, owner, classification, and quality score.
Add recommendations (related assets, frequently used together).
Build the browse interface organized by domain and taxonomy.

steps.description: Set up data lineage visualization across the catalog.

inputs.name: asset-inventory
inputs.desc: Inventory including ETL and transformation jobs

outputs.name: lineage-graph
outputs.desc: Data lineage graph (table and column level)

outputs.name: impact-analysis
outputs.desc: Ability to trace downstream impact of changes

process: Extract lineage from ETL tools, SQL parsing, and pipeline DAGs.
Build the lineage graph at table and column granularity.
Implement upstream and downstream traversal for impact analysis.
Visualize lineage paths in the catalog interface.

steps.description: Assign data owners and stewards and produce the catalog plan.

outputs.name: ownership-assignments
outputs.desc: Data owners and stewards for each domain

process: Assign data owners for each domain or dataset.
Define stewardship responsibilities (metadata curation, quality monitoring).
Set up the governance workflow for metadata changes and access requests.
Write the data catalog plan with rollout schedule and success metrics.
